Hi Marcus —

We're finalizing our internal forecasting for the POC and procurement asked for explicit counting examples so they can validate the budget line items. A couple of very specific scenarios we need clarified for the hosted API rate card and any baseline pricing/rounding rules you apply:

1) System prompts: we set a ~600-token system instruction per conversation start (persona + constraints). Does that count as input tokens for billing each request, or only once per session/connection? If we open many short-lived conversations, how should procurement model that?

2) Function/tool calls: we use a retrieval plugin that returns ~800 tokens of context; the model then synthesizes a 400-token answer that includes parts of the retrieved content. Are the retrieval/tool tokens billed as output, input, or both? If the retrieval content is large but the model returns a much shorter summary, how is that reflected on the invoice?

3) Streaming & partial responses: sometimes the model streams output in chunks. Are partial chunks rounded per-chunk (and billed) or only final-combined token counts are used? Any practical examples we can show to procurement?

4) Caching/KV: we expect to use prefix caching for a large static context. If a token exists in KV cache rather than sent in the request, do we still pay for it?

5) Rounding: does Redwood round up to the nearest token per API call, or is billing aggregated at a request/session/month level with different rounding behavior?

Can you provide example math for a plausible monthly footprint: say 1M user-input tokens, 2.5M model-output tokens, 50k system tokens, and 125k tool-result tokens — with and without a 20% committed discount?

Also, procurement wants a one-page sample invoice showing line items (input, output, system, tool, discount). If you can attach a small worksheet as well that shows the token->cost math, that’d be ideal.

Thanks — we’re trying to get the contract wrapped up next week.

Hi Sam / team — thanks, this is a great set of questions. Below are concise billing rules and then worked examples using the volumes you provided. I attached a sample invoice PDF and a workbook that spells out every line.

Short answers (policy):
- System messages: billed as input tokens. System text that you include as part of the request payload is tokenized by the same tokenizer and charged as input. If you keep system text on the client and do not send it in the request payload, it is not billed.

- Retrieval / tool outputs: billing depends on how the content is delivered to the model. If the retrieval plugin/tool returns content that is then included in the model message (i.e., the model receives the retrieved text as part of the request), those tokens are billed on the input side (because they are part of what the model consumes). If the model itself calls a function and the function returns data inside the model flow (model-generated function response), those returned tokens are billed as output. In many common setups the external retrieval is fetched server-side and then included in the prompt you send to the model — that is billed as input.

- Function call JSON / structured tool responses: counted as output tokens when generated by the model. If you call a tool that produces text outside the model (external service returns text but you do not pass it to the model), Redwood does not bill for tokens generated by that external service unless you include that content in requests to the model.

- Streaming: tokens are charged as they are emitted by the model. We charge by whole tokens — there is no fractional-token billing. Streaming does not cause double-billing beyond the tokens actually emitted; if a token is emitted once, it's billed once. There is no per-chunk rounding that increases counts beyond the actual tokenizer count for emitted tokens.

- Caching / KV: billing is based on what is transmitted to the model. If you rely on a runtime-side KV cache that avoids sending the full prefix for subsequent requests, you are only billed for the tokens you actually transmit. If you transmit a `context` field that references a cached object id and the runtime expands it implicitly without sending tokens, those expanded tokens are not billed to you. (Note: this behavior depends on the integration pattern; we advise validating with our solutions team during integration.)

Rounding & aggregation:
- We compute token counts at the per-request level using the model tokenizer and round to whole tokens. Billing sums the whole-token counts across requests for the invoice period; there is no additional per-request rounding up beyond tokenization rounding.

Worked example (your sample monthly footprint):
Assumptions for the calculation:
- Rate (hosted baseline): input tokens = $0.00009 per token; output tokens = $0.00018 per token; system tokens use the input rate. (These are illustrative baseline numbers — your committed price may differ.)
- Monthly volumes (from your note):
  • user-input tokens = 1,000,000
  • model-output tokens = 2,500,000
  • system tokens (persisting per-conversation start) = 50,000
  • tool/retrieval tokens included in requests = 125,000 (assumed sent as input)

Step 1 — raw token totals by side:
- Input-side tokens = user-input (1,000,000) + system (50,000) + retrieval-as-input (125,000) = 1,175,000 tokens
- Output-side tokens = model-output (2,500,000) [plus any model-generated function responses included in output; not assumed here] = 2,500,000 tokens

Step 2 — cost before discount:
- Input cost = 1,175,000 * $0.00009 = $105.75
- Output cost = 2,500,000 * $0.00018 = $450.00
- Subtotal = $555.75

Step 3 — apply committed discount (example 20% off total):
- Discount amount = $555.75 * 0.20 = $111.15
- Total after discount = $444.60

Notes on tool-generated content that is only returned to your app (not sent back to the model): those tokens do not appear on the Redwood usage invoice unless they are sent as part of a request to the model or are emitted by the model as output.

Invoice structure (what procurement will see):
- Line 1: Hosted API — input tokens (1,175,000) @ $0.00009 = $105.75
- Line 2: Hosted API — output tokens (2,500,000) @ $0.00018 = $450.00
- Line 3: Committed discount (20%) = -$111.15
- Line 4: Taxes / fees (as applicable)
- Total due = $444.60

Attached I included: acme_sample_invoice_q1.pdf (a one-page invoice stub) and sample_count_workbook.xlsx (token->cost math so procurement can tweak volumes and discount levels).

Practical tips for procurement modeling:
- If you can push static system text to the client and avoid sending it on every short interaction, you reduce input tokens.
- For retrieval-heavy flows, prefer server-side retrieval that only sends the minimal context the model needs (or use a summary step) — avoid sending full documents whenever possible.
- Streaming will not inflate counts beyond true tokenizer tokens; you can model output tokens conservatively by assuming an average output length per request.

If you want, Laura and I can run your actual request logs through our metering calculator and produce a pre-bill estimate that matches your projected traffic pattern. That will also surface any edge cases tied to function-calls versus retrieval integration patterns.

Best,
